correctness.rationale: For n>40, length-two sums mod n coincide exactly with integer sums. Legal sums a+b in S contribute triangle boundaries; for illegal sums, the integral kernel of the forbidden chord coefficient is generated by differences of ordered pairs with equal sum, contributing square boundaries. Thus H_1 is the first homology of the finite CW presentation with those 2-cells. The one-vertex voltage base Y_S has commutators from opposite step orderings and hence abelian pi_1=Q_S; its connected n-fold covering K_n has pi_1=ker(Q_S->Z/n). Independently enumerating the 28 unordered pair sums yielded the six short-relations; exact SymPy Smith form of the 6x7 integer matrix was diag(1,1,1,1,1,2), with maximal-minor absolute values (2,18,20,26,30,34,40). Each row has zero step-weight; the E15-15 E1 parity class has order exactly 2. Thus Q_S=Z⊕Z/2 and its reduction-mod-n kernel also Z⊕Z/2. Finite field boundary checks in the source are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: Stable integral 2-torsion in H_1 of strongly connected vertex-transitive circulants is invisible to rational Betti numbers and persists for prime moduli. The explicit small seven-step additive relation system is a motivated integral invariant and a counterexample to any assumption that such high-symmetry stable families are torsion-free. This is not a textbook exercise merely because an SNF calculation is finite.
